messages:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout: runtime v2.14 -> canary (10% traffic). deploy-id=deploy-1965432100. Monitoring p50/p95/p99.
Alex R: getting noise from dashboards — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms on canary clusters, error rate up. Paging oncall.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED (P1): runtime latency regression on canary (deploy-1965432100). Auto-alert threshold breached: p95 > 300ms for 5m.
Maria G (oncall): I'm looking. Pulling logs and kernel metrics now. Which pool is this hitting?
Alex R: canary pool: us-west-2-canary-1. Metric show many hosts flipped to "kernel_fallback" state and CPU steal spiked.
Priya S: if hosts are in kernel_fallback we might be hitting a new kernel scheduling path from v2.14 that regresses throughput under certain sequence lengths.
Kiran (eng-runtime): Confirmed. Trace samples show sequence of ops causing repeated kernel-selection thrash and higher syscalls per token. Batching keeps piling up so tail latency amplifies.
Maria G: Quick mitigations: 1) kill the kernel scheduler feature flag for canary, 2) disable continuous batching for canary route, 3) if needed, rollback the deploy. Which is fastest?
Sam T: feature flag flip is fastest. I can run config change now. Also recommend temporarily setting routing rule to divert canary traffic to fallback pool to reduce customer impact.
Sam T: Command I'm about to run: 
```
redwoodctl feature-set kernel_scheduler false --env canary --deploy=immediate --by=SamT
```
Maria G: Also reduce batch size to 1 for canary via kv: 
```
redwoodctl config set canary.batch.max_tokens 1 --env canary
```
Sam T: Running flag flip now...
deploy-bot: feature-change accepted: kernel_scheduler=false for env=canary (actor=SamT). Propagating to control plane.
oncall-sre: Observability: within 30s of flag flip p95 dropped ~40%. Error rate trending down but still above baseline.
Kiran (eng-runtime): I've disabled continuous batching for canary workers and forced kernel affinity back to legacy on those hosts. Patching in flight.
Maria G: Customers impacted: 0.6% of overall requests hit canary. Of those, approx 10% returned 504/timeouts during the 12m spike -> ~0.06% of total traffic. I notified paging for any high-traffic customers we know on canary.
Alex R: Noted a handful of internal integration tests still failing with KV cache misses — probably related to concurrent evictions during fallback. Tracking separately.
Priya S: If the flag and batching change don't fully recover in 10m we should rollback the deploy to previous stable.
Maria G: Timeline so far: 14:12 UTC deploy started. 14:18 alert triggered. 14:20 feature flag flip executed. 14:23 batching disabled. 14:30 p95 close to baseline but tail still noisy.
Sam T: I started a controlled rollback playbook just in case: 
```
# rollback plan (manual)
redwoodctl deploy rollback --id deploy-1965432100 --to v2.13 --reason "canary latency regression"
```
Kiran (eng-runtime): no rollback yet. Let the flags settle 10 more minutes and monitor. Kernel fallback eviction TTLs are ~45s; hosts should stabilize after current sessions drain.
oncall-sre: Handoff: Maria (14:50 UTC) -> Priya. Priya will own ongoing monitoring and customer comms until we close.
Priya S: Taking over. I'll open a post-incident ticket and start collecting traces + eval prompt sets that reproduce the length distribution.
Alex R: FYI I'm collecting per-route traces and will attach to the postmortem. Also logging exact host IDs that flipped to fallback.
Maria G: Closing actions for now: 1) keep feature flag off for canary, 2) keep batching disabled on canary routes, 3) run canary for additional 30m and then either revive with a config merge or rollback.
incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: incident-1965432100 created. Severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 after mitigations. Owner: Priya S.
Priya S: I'll draft customer-impact notes and schedule a blameless postmortem. Ticket: INC-1965432100.
Maria G: Thanks team. If tail latency resurges ping this thread and we can trigger immediate rollback. :thumbsup:
